facts.statement: Gryphoceratops was an extinct ceratopsian dinosaur belonging to the family Leptoceratopsidae, found in Alberta, southern Canada.
facts.quote: Gryphoceratops is an extinct genus of leptoceratopsid ceratopsian dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, southern Canada.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Gryphoceratops is a partial right dentary bone designated as holotype ROM 56635.
facts.quote: Gryphoceratops is known only from the holotype ROM 56635, a partial right dentary.

facts.statement: The holotype was discovered in bonebed 55 of the Milk River Formation within Dinosaur Provincial Park, dating to approximately 83 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype was collected in the northwest corner of Dinosaur Provincial Park, from bonebed 55 of the Milk River Formation, dating to the late Santonian stage of the middle Late Cretaceous period, about 83 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus Gryphoceratops was first named by Michael J. Ryan, David C. Evans, Philip J. Currie, Caleb M. Brown, and Don Brinkman in 2012.
facts.quote: Gryphoceratops was first named by Michael J. Ryan, David C. Evans, Philip J. Currie, Caleb M. Brown and Don Brinkman in 2012

facts.statement: Gryphoceratops is considered the oldest-known member of the leptoceratopsid family.
Despite being the oldest known leptoceratopsid, a cladistic analysis suggests it was one of the most advanced members of the group.
facts.quote: However, a cladistic analysis found it to be one of the most advanced leptoceratopsids.

facts.statement: The holotype likely represents the smallest known adult ceratopsian from North America.
facts.quote: Additionally, the holotype probably represents the smallest adult ceratopsian known from North America.

facts.statement: Gryphoceratops lived during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus name means "griffin horned face" referring to its beaked head, while the species name honors Ian Morrison, who prepared the holotype.
rejected.quote: The genus name means "griffin horned face", as a reference to the beaked head, and the species name honors Ian Morrison, who prepared the holotype specimen.
